key_insight: The classical 2-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm stabilizes in linear time, with a proven upper bound of 5(n-1) rounds, closing the gap to the known Ω(n) lower bound.
engineering_relevance: This sharpens the runtime guarantees for a foundational graph refinement procedure used in graph isomorphism, structural graph analysis, and related algebraic/combinatorial pipelines.
method: Analyze the stabilization behavior of the classical 2-WL refinement process.
Prove a new worst-case upper bound of 5(n-1) iterations.
Extend the argument to k-WL for k≥3, yielding improved bounds O(n^{k-1}/(k-2)! + n^{k-2}).
evidence_signal: The paper provides theoretical worst-case iteration bounds and compares them against the previous O(n log n) upper bound and the known Ω(n) lower bound.
watch_item: The result is about iteration complexity, not total wall-clock runtime, so practical performance still depends on implementation and per-round cost.
paper_title: The Classical Weisfeiler-Leman Algorithm Stabilizes in $O(n)$ Rounds
